authority: Owner entry approval of ASM-0089 at its exact current text, epic #1201 (ADR-MCPRE-070) assurance closure
text:
[[assumption]]
id = "ASM-0089"
description = "A commitment provider registered for the required audit posture returns a receipt for an event only once that event is committed at the durability tier the provider declared, and the declared tier holds under the fault model it names — at minimum, loss of the proxy process (`SURVIVES_PROXY_PROCESS_LOSS`, `audit-durability/v1`)."
justification = """
THM-0135 and THM-0136 say the proxy dispatches and serves success only while it holds a
redeemed witness, and a witness is minted only from a receipt that names the event identity,
content digest, crossing kind and declared tier the shared owner SENT. That a receipt also
means the event persists is the provider's fact: the provider is an independently compiled
implementation behind `CommitmentAuthority`, and nothing in the process can observe its
storage (ADR-MCPRE-070 §9, D3). An `Ok`, a receipt type, or a Rust proof never establishes it.

What stays this project's and is tested here: the receipt-to-envelope match, single
redemption against this event and this established provider instance, the bounded wait and
the typed failures, the closed tier vocabulary and its minimum, and the startup refusal of a
required posture without an established qualifying provider (`proxy.audit_commitment_witness`,
`proxy.audit_posture`). The open-source binary registers no provider, and the test-only
reference authority — process memory — is not a provider this premise covers; every build a
deployment runs refuses it.

It stops being acceptable for a provider that answers on network receipt or replicated
acceptance rather than stable commitment — an `XADD` reply, a Redis `WAIT`, a TCP
acknowledgement, a collector's HTTP 2xx (ADR-MCPRE-070 §3) — or that declares a tier its
mechanism does not meet. A lying or Byzantine provider is outside the model and cannot be
detected by the shared code. No claim of exactly-once delivery or of unconditional
permanence rests on this premise.
"""
scope = [
  "unit://proxy.audit_commitment_witness",
  "unit://proxy.audit_intent_gate",
  "unit://proxy.audit_outcome_gate",
  "unit://proxy.audit_posture",
  "boundary://boundary.audit_commitment_provider",
]
owner = "mats@sundvall.name"
introduced_by = "#1207 (ADR-MCPRE-070 D3, D10, P9)"
review_requirement = "Owner review on any change to the CommitmentAuthority seam, the receipt-to-witness binding, the tier vocabulary or its minimum, and on registering any provider for the required posture."
premise_class = "external-boundary"
boundary_owner = """
The embedder that compiles and registers a `CommitmentAuthority` for `--audit-commitment
required`, across `CommitmentAuthority::commit` and `CommitmentAuthority::declared_tier`: a
receipt is returned only once the event it names is committed at the declared tier, and that
tier survives at least the loss of the proxy process under the provider's declared fault
model. Qualification is per provider, with mechanism evidence of its own.
"""
affected_contracts = []
sites = [
  "mcp-re-proxy/src/audit_commitment/authority.rs#CommitmentAuthority",
]
tool_specific_mechanism = "none:trusted-seam"

authority: Owner entry approval of ASM-0090 at its exact current text, epic #1201 (ADR-MCPRE-070) assurance closure
text:
[[assumption]]
id = "ASM-0090"
description = "A required deployment's commitment provider answers within the configured commitment bound and recovers after an outage, and a committed event reaches the downstream archive only through a transport that delivers it at least once and an archive that takes custody before anything is trimmed."
justification = """
This is the condition of liveness, never of safety. THM-0135 and THM-0136 hold during any
outage: an exchange whose intent or outcome cannot be committed is refused, before dispatch
with a disposition that never states a success (`NothingExecuted`, or
`ApprovalSpentNothingExecuted` where a continuation approval was already spent) or after it
with `PossiblyExecuted`, and that refusal is the claim
working, not failing. That a required exchange eventually SUCCEEDS needs the provider to
answer inside the bound and to come back after it stops (ADR-MCPRE-070 L1). That a committed
event is eventually ARCHIVED needs the downstream transport, its consumers and the archive to
behave as the deployment declares (L3, P10). Neither is something the proxy can do or observe,
and neither is ever a test result.

Downstream delivery is at-least-once: a retried delivery carries the same event identity and
bytes, and consumers deduplicate on the event binding (identity and digest), never on a
transport position such as a stream ID (§8, §12). There is no exactly-once delivery, no
global order across runs, and no unconditional permanence.

It stops being acceptable as a statement of what a deployment gets if the deployment trims or
expires committed events before archive custody, deduplicates on transport position, or reads
a missing archive entry as an event that never happened.
"""
scope = [
  "unit://proxy.audit_commitment_witness",
  "unit://proxy.audit_intent_gate",
  "unit://proxy.audit_outcome_gate",
  "unit://proxy.audit_posture",
  "boundary://boundary.audit_commitment_provider",
]
owner = "mats@sundvall.name"
introduced_by = "#1207 (ADR-MCPRE-070 D10, L1, L3, P10)"
review_requirement = "Owner review on any change to the commitment bound, to the refusal a failed commitment earns, or to the documented downstream delivery contract."
premise_class = "external-boundary"
boundary_owner = """
The deployment operator together with the registered provider, across
`CommitmentAuthority::commit` and whatever transport carries committed events to an archive:
the provider answers within the configured commitment bound and recovers after an outage, the
transport delivers every committed event at least once, consumers deduplicate on the event
binding, and the archive takes custody before any committed event is trimmed.
"""
affected_contracts = []
tool_specific_mechanism = "none"

authority: Owner entry approval of ASM-0091 at its exact current text, epic #1201 (ADR-MCPRE-070) assurance closure
text:
[[assumption]]
id = "ASM-0091"
description = "The commitment provider's capacity is finite, and a required deployment makes progress only while that capacity covers the commitment rate it offers within its commitment budget."
justification = """
Capacity is finite on both sides and the safety claims assume nothing else. The proxy bounds
its own demand: commitments hold a try-acquired budget that is separate from the observer's
queue and from the retention reservations, and each crossing makes one bounded attempt. One
budget per established provider is shared by G1, G2 and the accounting cadence. At G1 a spent
budget or a saturated provider is refused before dispatch with a retry-safe 503. At G2 the
same saturation is a 500 `PossiblyExecuted` refusal AFTER dispatch: the backend call has run
and its success is withheld (ADR-MCPRE-070 §7). At the accounting cadence it is a missed
interval, and no request is refused. Under saturation THM-0135 and THM-0136 still hold,
because nothing is dispatched or served as success without a witness. What does not hold is
progress: a provider whose capacity is below the offered rate turns admitted exchanges into
refusals, and some of those refusals follow an execution.

Sizing the provider against the deployment's commitment rate is the operator's and the
provider's, and nothing in the proxy can establish it. Individual unauthenticated and
pre-exchange attempts are never committed (D2), so they do not draw on this capacity; the
aggregate `mcp-re.audit.accounting` record does, once per interval, and states a missed
interval rather than waiting.

It stops being acceptable as a statement of what a deployment gets if the budget ceiling is
raised above what the provider can answer within the bound, or if a provider queues
commitments past the bound instead of answering Unavailable.
"""
scope = [
  "unit://proxy.audit_intent_gate",
  "unit://proxy.audit_outcome_gate",
  "unit://proxy.audit_posture",
  "boundary://boundary.audit_commitment_provider",
]
owner = "mats@sundvall.name"
introduced_by = "#1207 (ADR-MCPRE-070 D2, D10, §7)"
review_requirement = "Owner review on any change to the commitment budget, its ceiling, or the accounting cadence."
premise_class = "external-boundary"
boundary_owner = """
The deployment operator and the registered provider, across `CommitmentAuthority::commit`:
the provider is sized for the commitment rate the deployment offers within its budget, and
answers Unavailable, rather than holding a commitment past the bound, when it is not.
"""
affected_contracts = []
tool_specific_mechanism = "none"

authority: Owner entry approval of ASM-0092 at its exact current text, epic #1201 (ADR-MCPRE-070) assurance closure
text:
[[assumption]]
id = "ASM-0092"
description = "rustls, over the whole public Web PKI root set the pinned `webpki-roots` 1.x crate ships, completes an outbound agent's handshake only for a server certificate that chains to one of those roots, names the destination host the agent connected to, and is inside its validity window at the handshake, presented by a server that proved possession of that certificate's private key; and the certificate authorities in that root set issue a certificate for a name only to the party that controls it."
justification = """
THM-0090 says a credential leaves this proxy only to the endpoint its rule admitted. The rule
admits a NAME. That the server answering on the socket is the holder of that name is decided
by TLS server authentication, and since RUSTSEC-2026-0381/-0382 the proxy installs that
authentication itself: `VettedDestination::agent` builds every outbound agent with
`RootedConnector::public()` (`mcp-re-proxy/src/outbound_fetch/public_roots.rs`), a rustls
client on the ring provider, safe default protocol versions, no client certificate, over a
`RootCertStore` holding exactly `webpki_roots::TLS_SERVER_ROOTS`, with the URL host ureq
connected to as the server name. Those choices are this repository's and are tested (NP-290's
controls CD-20600..20603): a server under a trusted root completes the handshake and carries
bytes; a server under a private CA is refused as `UnknownIssuer` before any request byte; the
store is the whole shipped set; a host that is not a server name is refused. ureq is built
without its `tls` feature, so an agent without this connector refuses https rather than
authenticating under another root set.

Two facts are not this repository's, and this entry is both of them. First, that rustls and
webpki check what the handshake reports: path building to a shipped root, the name match, the
validity window, the CertificateVerify proof of key possession. That is the same mechanism
premise ASM-0070 states for the client transport, but over a different root set and for a
different unit. Second, and only here: the trust boundary is EXTERNAL. Every certificate
authority in the shipped set, the Mozilla root program as `webpki-roots` packages it, is
trusted to issue for any name. A mis-issued certificate under any one of them authenticates a
server this proxy then sends a credential to. Nothing in the process can detect that.

This is distinct from ASM-0070 and does not widen it. ASM-0070's roots are the ones an
operator configured for one proxy. These are a public set the operator never named, chosen
when the crate version is pinned. A change to one says nothing about the other.

Not claimed: revocation (`with_root_certificates` builds the verifier without revocation, so
a revoked, unexpired certificate under a shipped root is accepted); Certificate Transparency;
that the shipped set is current (a CA distrusted after the pinned release is trusted until the
pin moves, as RUSTSEC-2026-0381 was); pinning to any particular CA or key; and any property of
the destination beyond holding a certificate for its name.

It stops being acceptable if an outbound agent installs any connector or verifier other than
`RootedConnector::public()` in a production build, if its root store is populated from anything
but the whole `webpki-roots` set, if a client certificate or a custom verifier is added, or on
any change to the pinned rustls, rustls-webpki or webpki-roots version.
"""
scope = [
  "unit://proxy.outbound_destination",
  "boundary://boundary.tls_mechanism",
]
owner = "mats@sundvall.name"
introduced_by = "Owner ruling 2026-10-21, epic #1201 final authority closure, direction 6 (NP-290)"
review_requirement = "Owner review on any change to how an outbound agent's TLS is built (connector, verifier, root store, client authentication), or to the pinned rustls, rustls-webpki or webpki-roots version."
premise_class = "external-boundary"
boundary_owner = """
rustls with webpki path validation, across `RootedConnector::public()` as built in
`mcp-re-proxy/src/outbound_fetch/public_roots.rs`, and the certificate authorities of the public
Web PKI root set the pinned `webpki-roots` 1.x crate ships: a handshake completes only for a
server certificate that chains to a shipped root, matches the destination host, is within its
validity window, and is presented by a server holding its private key; and a shipped CA issues
for a name only to the party that controls it.
"""
affected_contracts = []
tool_specific_mechanism = "foreign-dependency"

authority: Owner ruling, epic #1201 (ADR-MCPRE-070) assurance closure: ratification of the 70 re-reviews; re-acknowledgement of ASM-0070 and ASM-0082
text:
**OWNER RULING — APPROVED**

I ratify the 70 re-reviews documented in `verification/reviews/packets/epic-1201-assurance-closure-2026-10-21.md` (57 CLEAN, 13 CLEAN-NOTE, zero false claims; THM-0122 and THM-0101 corrected) and the agent-prepared specification records written at the identities that packet and `verification/reviews/rulings/epic-1201-authority-closure-2026-10-21.md` name. The evidence class of each theorem is as registered; V0 evidence is tests and probes, not machine-checked proof.

I re-acknowledge ASM-0070 and ASM-0082 at their current, unchanged entry text after the RUSTSEC-2026-0381/-0382 remediation: rustls-webpki 0.103.16 narrows path validation, and the outbound agent's own TLS connector changes neither the destination ureq connects to nor redirect handling. Server authentication by that connector is ASM-0092.
